# Zerble

> Zerble is an art cart: a real golf cart with giant googly eyes and a fluffy purple mustache, sketched on a napkin in 2011 and a festival fixture ever since, including LEAF in Black Mountain, North Carolina. Zerble is co-owned by Gary Reckard and Locke Crawford, lives in a garage in West Asheville, has a page in the LEAF book Live Life Like a Festival, and stars in a free browser game, Zerble at the Festival.

## History

- 2011: Gary Reckard was building MagBuds, a volunteer registration system for the festivals at the Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park in Florida (including Magnolia Fest and SpringFest), when he learned he'd be getting his own golf cart at the fest. He got the news at Mo Daddy's in Asheville, North Carolina, and sketched Zerble on a napkin.
- 2011: The first eyeballs were blue marbled bouncy balls from Kmart, primed white everywhere but the iris, with headlamps taped to the back. They were mounted on the roof corners like a snail's eyes, on a green golf cart with a mustache cut from black posterboard and a MAG BUDS sign.
- 2011 to 2016, the Suwannee years: Zerble scooted around the Spirit of the Suwannee Music Park festivals (Magnolia Fest, SpringFest, Bear Creek, and Wanee), hauling gear, shuttling musicians, and blowing bubbles. Zerble was rebuilt for each fest with a new set of eyes, a new mustache, and other accessories, and the mustache began to glow. By Bear Creek in November 2014, the mustache had gone fuzzy and purple, with a fancy bow tie.
- 2016, Florida to North Carolina: Zerble's build kept evolving (experimental eyeball mounts, the occasional schnoz, even a cow and a monkey), and Zerble started showing up at North Carolina festivals too, like the French Broad River Festival in Hot Springs.
- May 2016: Before buying a cart of their own, Gary and Locke Crawford rented one and built a Zerble at the French Broad River Festival.
- Later in 2016: Gary and Locke bought a red EZ-GO off Craigslist and built the version of Zerble that's still rolling today. The eyes moved inward from their snail-like perch to a central dashboard mount, the mustache got an upgrade, and Locke was the mastermind behind much of the wiring (dashboard switches and USB ports all over). The bubble machine has been through many iterations, since few bubble machines last more than one festival. From then on, Zerble has been a fixture at every LEAF.
- July 1, 2017: Zerble carried Gary and Fox at their wedding in Old Fort, North Carolina.
- October 2017: For Fall LEAF, Locke Crawford made a limited run of unique, custom mini Zerble toys, packaged each one with an official Certificate of Authenticity, and delivered them to special people at the festival.
- May 2018: Gary made a rare, limited-edition batch of "I Rode Zerble" buttons to give out at Spring LEAF.
- Fall 2019: For Fall LEAF, Gary and Locke designed special wooden Zerble Fan Club tokens, laser-engraved every one of them on a cheap engraver, and handed them out to special people at the fest.
- Thanksgiving 2019: Zerble visited Fort Wilderness Resort & Campground at Walt Disney World.
- 2020: Gary's son Darwin was born on March 25, 2020, just as COVID shut everything down. Locke had already built an RC Zerble for the baby shower, and Darwin soon joined the crew in a Zerble onesie Locke made.
- October 2022: Zerble fell in behind ToyBox and joined the parade.
- 2023: The Zerble onesie came back out for Gary's daughter, Zelda, the second Zerblet to wear it.
- May 11, 2024: Zerble lit up under a rare appearance of the northern lights over LEAF.
- May 2025: Jami got a Zerble tattoo in the Retro Zerble design.
- October 2025: Zerble and Lurleen, Zerble's sweetheart, shared their first kiss.
- May 2026: Gary started building the browser game Zerble at the Festival.
- October 2, 2026: Zerble ran shuttle duty at the East-West Asheville Fall Art Walk, organized by Lamplight AVL (https://lamplightavl.org/artwalks/).
- Up next: the Lake Eden Reunion.

## About Zerble

- Zerble is a golf cart decorated with enormous blue googly eyes and a big purple mustache.
- Zerble is owned equally by Gary Reckard and Locke Crawford and lives in a garage in West Asheville, North Carolina.
- Zerble's sweetheart is Lurleen, a real art cart brought to life by Locke Crawford, with puffy pink lips, raffia hair, and a crown of flowers. She lives in the same garage as Zerble.
- Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/zerble_art_cart/ (@zerble_art_cart), with photos of the real cart at festivals and plenty of art.
- Spotted Zerble? Fans who have a photo of Zerble, or a selfie with the cart, can post it on Instagram with the hashtag #zerble and tag @zerble_art_cart.
- Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/Zerble (updated less often than Instagram).

## The bubble fund

- Zerble's bubble machine runs on pro-grade bubble juice. A box of four one-gallon jugs costs about $90, and a single festival can use one or two of those jugs.
- Fans can tip toward bubble juice on Venmo (@zerble, https://venmo.com/zerble) from https://zerble.net/#bubble-juice, with suggested amounts of $5, $10, $25 (about a gallon), and $90 (a whole box).
- Zerble isn't a charity, so tips aren't tax-deductible.

## The handlers

- Gary Reckard: co-owner and handler. Zerble was his brainchild, born down on the Suwannee River, and he made the eyes, the mustache, and the bubble machine mount. He also built the browser game.
- Locke Crawford: co-owner and handler. Locke did much of the wiring, brought Lurleen to life, and throws a lot of the party, including golf-cart karaoke, surprise dance parties, and mobile brass band parades.

## In the book: Live Life Like a Festival

- Zerble has a page in Live Life Like a Festival by Jennifer Pickering, a coffee table book celebrating 30 years of LEAF Global Arts.
- The book is available for pre-order: https://www.jenniferpickering.com/shop/p/live-like-a-festival-book
- About the book: https://www.jenniferpickering.com/book

## Merch

- Zerble's art is for sale on Redbubble, which prints and ships every order: https://www.redbubble.com/people/garbonzo00/shop?collections=4591699
- The designs are Happy Bubbles (https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/184500818), Neon Monster (https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/184501916), Pixel Zerble (https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/184500387), Retro Zerble (https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/142133371), and Zerble & Lurleen (https://www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/184502727).
- Products include tees, hoodies, stickers, pins, throw pillows, phone cases, posters, and more, depending on the design.

## The game: Zerble at the Festival

- Play free in any modern web browser, on a laptop or a phone, with nothing to install: https://garyreckard.github.io/zerble-at-the-festival/
- You drive Zerble through a procedural festival that builds itself as you go (stages, food trucks, drum circles, lakes, and forests) and trail bubbles past the crowd to collect smiles.
- The game's tagline: "Bring the bubbles, collect the smiles."
- Two modes: Just Cruisin' (endless, no pressure) and Festival Run (each festival day brings scarcer bubble juice and stricter marshals).
- Controls: WASD to drive on a keyboard (arrow keys orbit the camera, Shift boosts, Space honks the horn), or the on-screen thumbstick and buttons on a phone.
- Lurleen is in the game too, and if you drive up to her slowly, the air fills with hearts.
- Built by Gary Reckard, starting in May 2026, with three.js and Web Audio and no build step.
